text:
steve_acme: Hey team — we're seeing truncated SSE responses from /v1/stream. The stream ends abruptly after a reconnect and the final JSON object is incomplete. finish_reason is null and there's no final data: [DONE] event. Happened ~10:32 PST after our token rotation. Sample tail:

data: {\"id\":\"abc\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"},\"finish_reason\":null}

...and it just stops. Request id rwd-9f2a. Repro with curl on our side. Any ideas?

alex: Thanks — can you paste the raw SSE stream (first/last ~1KB) and the request headers? especially Last-Event-ID or any resume headers. Also confirm if there's an edge/proxy in front of your client.

steve_acme: Pasted snippet above (that's the tail). Headers we saw: Last-Event-ID: 12345, Authorization was rotating (we saw intermittent 401s ~10:30). We're behind Fastly -> nginx -> app.

maria: Do you use a resume header when reconnecting? i.e. Last-Event-ID or a custom Redwood-Resume? Also, does your client attempt an immediate reconnect or exponential backoff?

jamal: Sounds like a proxy/buffer flush issue. If Fastly or nginx buffers the last chunk, and the client reconnects while token rotate triggers a 401/redirect, the final flush can be dropped. Can you run a repro with curl --no-buffer to capture exact SSE frames? Also check server is setting X-Accel-Buffering: no.

steve_acme: Running curl now. Quick note: client reconnected immediately when it got 401 from our refresh service. We do send Last-Event-ID on reconnect.

support-bot: Ticket created RWI-4532 (priority: P2) — assigned to jamal.

alex: Short-term mitigation: make clients tolerant of missing finish_reason — treat abrupt EOF as a terminal condition if no more frames arrive for N seconds, then attempt resume based on Last-Event-ID. Long-term: server should always emit an explicit terminator (data: [DONE] + final JSON with finish_reason) and ensure flush semantics over proxies.

jamal: Reproduced locally: Fastly idle timeout + nginx proxy buffering + an auth rotation during the tail causes the final chunk to be dropped. Repro steps: 1) start streaming (curl --no-buffer) 2) trigger token rotation while stream in progress 3) client reconnects -> final chunk is missing, JSON truncated. Observed identical behavior.

jamal: Immediate recommended fixes: set nginx/proxy to disable response buffering and ensure SSE-friendly headers. Example nginx tweaks:

```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
sendfile off;
```

And increase Fastly / edge idle timeouts to avoid mid-stream connection termination. We'll push a staging config and test.

maria: I'll schedule a quick staging rollout of the nginx config and run the token-rotate repro. tagging ops for a controlled rollout window.

steve_acme: Thanks — after you push, can you provide a short set of repro steps I can run to verify from our side?

jamal: Yep — verified steps to validate after change:
1) start streaming from a client: curl -v --no-buffer -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?prompt=test'
2) in a second shell, run our token-rotation script to force a refresh event
3) watch the first terminal for the final `data:` frames — after fix you should see `data: [DONE]` and a complete JSON final chunk (finish_reason set). If you still see truncated JSON, send the curl output + request id.

maria: rolling to staging in 15m. will post results.

alex: :thumbsup:
